Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL MEETING

  June 25, 2019
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine , CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The special meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 3:04 p.m . on June
25, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza ,
Irvine, California ; Mayor Shea presiding .

ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Michael C. Carroll
  Council member:  Melissa Fox
  Council member:  Farrah N. Khan
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

Mayor Shea noted that in order to accommodate the three Closed Session items and six
presentations , the City Manager's Report, Additions and Deletions , and the Consent
Calendar would be considered prior to Closed Session .

1.  CLOSED SESSION

  This item was considered following the City Manager's Report, Additions and
  Deletions, and the Consent Calendar.
 City Council Minutes  June 25, 2019

  City Attorney Melching announced the following Closed Session items:

  1. 1  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LIT/GA TION -
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) - Housing is a
  Human Right v. City of Irvine, United States District Court, Central
  District of California Case No. 8:19-CV-388

  1.2  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LIT/GA TION -
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) -- City of Irvine
  vs. Unity Church, et al., Orange County Superior Court Case No. 30-
  2018-00988207

  1.3  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION -  Government
  Code Section 54957; Title : City Manager

  There were no requests to speak.

  RECESS

  Mayor Shea recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 3:13 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  Mayor Shea reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:31 p.m. and noted that the City
  Council would continue its Closed Session prior to adjournment.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Fox led the Pledge of Allegiance .

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Graham McGuinness from Woodbridge Community Church in Irvine provided the
  invocation .

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  Mayor Shea reordered the agenda to consider Presentation Item Nos. 2 .6 and 2.5
  prior to Presentation Item Nos. 2.1 through 2.4.

  2. 1  Emergency Management Overview

  Mayor Shea introduced Bobby Simmons, Emergency Management
  Administrator, and Michael Kent, Police Commander, who provided a brief
  overview of the City's emergency management.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  2
 City Council Minutes  June 25, 2019

  City Council discussion included : highlighting the use of goats to abate
  weeds in some of the City's open space ; and noted an upcoming Wildland
  Management Event, in partnership with the Orange County Fire Authority,
  in Quail Hill on July 20 from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. to highlight the goat program.

  2.2  Irvine Community Land Trust

  Mayor Shea introduced Mark Asturias, Executive Director, Irvine
  Community Land Trust (Land Trust), who provided an overview of the
  organization, its accomplishments to date, and future affordable housing
  projects.

  City Council discussion included : inquiring about pend ing legislation related
  to property taxation on affordable housing projects; and questioned
  whether the Land Trust partnered with Habitat Humanity of Orange County
  on the Native Springs project.

  Branda Lin , Irvine resident, expressed concern about costs related to
  staffing and marketing , as well as costs associated with new development
  projects versus rehabilitation of existing homes, and spoke in support of
  further enhancing transparency.

  Jeanne Baran , Irvine resident, spoke in support of increasing public access
  to Land Trust activities and financial documents.

  2.3  Southern California Edison Safari Substation Progress Update

  Karalee Darnell , Government Affairs Manager, Southern California Edison
  (SCE), and Jeff Davis , Vice President, Irvine Company, provided a brief
  update on the progress of the Safari Substation .

  Mike Aguirre , accompanied by business owners on Wald Street, expressed
  his appreciation to Mayor Shea and the City Council for their collaborative
  efforts with SCE and Irvine Company to relocate the Safari Substation.

  2.4  Southern California Edison Wildfire Mitigation Briefing

  Karalee Darnell , Government Affairs Manager, Southern California Ed ison,
  provided a brief update on wildfire mitigation , which included changes to
  operational practices and infrastructure advancement, as well as potential
  impacts to the City.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  3
 City Council Minutes  June 25, 2019

  City Council discussion included : inquiring about the causes of past
  wildfires across the state; discussed environmental differences between
  Northern and Southern California ; and reiterated that loss of homes and
  communities would be minimized through these efforts.

  2.5  Proclaim June 30, 2019 as "City of Irvine Day of Peace" and Designate
  Irvine as an "International City of Peace"

  Mayor Shea introduced Beth Fujishige, president of the Irvine Rotary Club;
  and invited Councilmember Khan , who recognized representatives from the
  following organizations, to present a proclamation recognizing June 30,
  2019 as "City of Irvine Day of Peace" and designating Irvine as an
  "International City of Peace":

  •  Irvine Kiwanis Club
  •  Irvine Exchange Club
  •  World Affairs Council of Orange County
  •  Irvine for All
  •  UC Irvine Center for Citizen Peace Building
  •  Korean American Center
  •  Friends of Outreach
  •  Newport Irvine Rotary
  •  Church of Latter Day Saints
  •  Orange County Formosan Association
  •  Ektaa Center
  •  Irvine Multicultural Association

  2.6  Commend Patrick Chung for Life-Saving Efforts

  Mayor Shea introduced Patrick Chung , Irvine resident, and expressed her
  appreciation for his life-saving efforts; and Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo
  presented a commendation recognizing Mr. Chung 's heroism. Beth
  Fujishige, on behalf of the Irvine Rotary Club, also presented Mr. Chung
  with a check for $250.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  4
 City Council Minutes  June 25, 2019

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  July is National Park and Recreation Month, and the Community Services
  Department has developed a calendar and web page highlighting different
  activities at City parks every day in July. Activities will also be posted each day on
  Facebook, Twitter, and lnstagram.

  •  Tickets are on sale for the Irvine Police Association 's 35 th annual Concert on the
  Green and Fireworks Festival on July 4 at the Irvine High School Stadium. The
  day includes live music, a food court, games and activities for children , and the
  presentation of the colors by the Irvine Police Department Honor Guard.
  Festivities begin at 3 p.m. and wrap up at 9 p.m . with a Musical Sky Concert and
  Fireworks Extravaganza.

  •  The Great Park Gallery is hosting an art exhibition that celebrates the iconic El
  Toro Air Show. In conjunction with the exhibition , there will be three concerts at
  the Palm Courts Arts Complex this summer featuring big band, Jazz, and swing
  music. The first concert is on Thursday, June 25 at 7 p.m. The art exhibition , "A
  Brief History of the El Toro Air Show: 1950 - 1997" features a series of graphic
  designs by artist Paul Gavin , who dedicated his career to the celebration of U.S.
  Armed Forces by contributing artwork to a number of military-related events,
  including the iconic El Toro Air Show of Orange County. The exhibition will be on
  display through August 18.

  •  The City's Sizzlin ' Summer Concert series return to Mike Ward Community Park -
  Woodbridge on Sunday, July 7 at 5:30 p.m. , with '80s tribute band Pop Gun
  Rerun . Gourmet food trucks and a children 's play area will also be available. The
  free , family-friendly concerts in the park run through August 11.

  •  On June 21 , the City hosted its annual Super Swim Lesson at the William Woollett
  Jr. Aquatics Center as part of an effort to raise awareness for drowning
  prevention . Parents and chi ldren were educated about water safety, and the
  message was spread that "Swimming Lessons Save Lives."

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  5
 City Council Minutes  Ju ne 25, 2019

  •  The City of Hope is investing more than $1 billion to develop a world-class cancer
  research and treatment campus in Irvine. Located on approximately 11 acres of
  land adjacent to the Orange County Great Park, the City of Hope campus will
  bring highly specialized cancer care, clinical trials, precision medicine, and early
  detection to the City and to the greater Orange County community. Nearly 20
  percent of cancer patients leave the area for advanced care. The new City of
  Hope center will provide patients with the benefit of much-needed personalized
  care, innovative research, and lifesaving treatments close to home as early as
  2021 . This adds another dimension to the progress and development at the
  Orange County Great Park in partnership with FivePoint.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  Councilmember Fox asked that Item 5.1 (Consideration of Councilmember Fox's
  Request to Adopt a Resolution Designating the Amended and Restated Development
  Agreement (ARDA) Site as the Appropriate Location for the Veterans Cemetery; and
  Expressing the City's Intent to Transfer the Property to the State) be continued to the
  August 13, 2019 City Council meeting.

  City Council discussion included: discussing alternative meeting dates due to scheduling
  conflicts, as well as requests by State representatives to consider the item in July; and
  suggested that the Great Park Chairwoman work with the City Manager to determine a
  date and time in July for City Council and Orange County Great Park Board discussion.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo, to:

  Continue Item 5.1 (Consideration of Councilmember Fox's Request
  to Adopt a Resolution Designating the Amended and Restated
  Development Agreement (ARDA) Site as the Appropriate Location
  for the Veterans Cemetery; and Expressing the City's Intent to
  Transfer the Property to the State) to a date to be determined in July
  by the Chairwoman of the Orange County Great Park Board and the
  City Manager.

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES :  4  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll , Khan , Kuo and
  Shea

  NOES:  1  COUNCILMEMBERS :  Fox

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS :  None

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  6
